claims.claim: On the Amex network, a 'partner' means a third party licensed by American Express as an Issuer or an Acquirer; no principal/affiliate tiering is published.
claims.quote: refers solely to third parties licensed as Issuers or Acquirers and does not mean or imply a formal legal partnership
claims.title: Welcome to the American Express Network
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Footer disclaimer on the GNS partner site. The site groups partners as Issuers, Acquirers, Fintechs, Service Providers and Developers. Copyright 2026.

claims.claim: Amex's 10-K describes its network partners as third-party banks and institutions licensed to issue Amex-branded cards and/or to acquire local merchants, in about 110 countries and territories.
claims.quote: These network partners are licensed to issue American Express-branded cards in their countries and/or serve as the merchant acquirer for local merchants on our network.
claims.title: American Express Company Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Preceding sentence read on the same page: 'we establish and maintain relationships with third-party banks and other institutions in approximately 110 countries and territories through our card network business'. FY2025 10-K, accession 0000004962-26-000080, filed 2026; postdates the Capital One/Discover close. Direct curl of sec.gov was blocked as an undeclared automated tool; content read via WebFetch.

claims.claim: Under OptBlue, third-party acquirers and processors, not Amex, contract directly with small merchants and set merchant pricing.
claims.quote: through our OptBlue® merchant-acquiring program, these third parties contract directly with small merchants for card acceptance on our network and determine merchant pricing
claims.title: American Express Company Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same filing: 'as of December 31, 2025, we had 66.2 million cards-in-force issued by third parties worldwide' and worldwide processed volume of $227.2 billion for 2025.

claims.claim: Amex's network segment (GMNS) lists a prepaid reloadable and gift card program manager as a third participant type alongside third-party issuers and acquirers.
claims.quote: manages partnership relationships with third-party card issuers, merchant acquirers and a prepaid reloadable and gift card program manager
claims.title: American Express Company Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Sentence surfaced in a search-index snippet of the 10-K; it did not appear in the portion the fetch tool returned, so it is labelled Reported. The program-manager reference is a single named relationship, not a published participation category.

claims.claim: Network rulebooks are handed to licensed Issuers and Acquirers only after they sign an agreement with American Express; there is no public application form or licensing checklist.
claims.quote: published manuals which are provided to licensed Issuers and Acquirers upon signing an agreement with American Express
claims.title: American Express Global Network Policy
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page also says the Business and Operational Policies (BOP) manual 'is a global document which is published bi-annually in April and October'. Next-step CTA for prospective participants is only 'Contact us' (web form).

claims.claim: The Amex network rulebook (BOP manual) is confidential and not publicly available, so partner obligations cannot be read before licensing.
claims.quote: The Business and Operational Policies (BOP) manual is a confidential document that contains sensitive proprietary information
claims.title: American Express Global Network Policy
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: FAQ 'Why is the Business and Operational Polices (BOP) manual not publically available?'. Contrast: Visa and Mastercard publish public-facing rule excerpts; Amex publishes only merchant-facing guides.

claims.claim: The BOP manual and Network Specifications are legally binding parts of each Issuer/Acquirer agreement; non-compliance can carry financial liability.
claims.quote: are an integral part of agreements executed between the American Express Global Network and Issuers and Acquirers
claims.title: American Express Global Network Policy
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Continues: 'failure to comply with policies and specifications may result in financial liabilities and legal action.' Policy updates arrive monthly via Network Participant Updates (NPU), second Friday of every month.

claims.claim: Network fees charged to participants are published only inside the confidential BOP manual; no public partner fee schedule exists.
claims.quote: Disputes processing rules Service establishment requirements that acquirers must enforce American Express Global Network fees
claims.title: American Express Global Network Policy
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Quote is three consecutive bullet items from the FAQ 'What does the Business and Operational Policies (BOP) manual contain?', flattened. Absence of any public licensing, certification or participation fee is a finding.

claims.claim: Acquirers must complete both host certification and POS terminal certification before submitting transactions to the Amex network.
claims.quote: acquirers must be certified to submit American Express transactions to the American Express Global Network, including certification of host and Point of Sale
claims.title: American Express Certification
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: POS device step: 'Submit the certification request form, including device information, to American Express relationship manager', provide device/card interaction logs and receipts, and perform test cases supplied by the relationship manager. No timelines or fees stated.

claims.claim: Issuers must complete host certification and payment product certification (card production, chip development, embedding, data prep, personalization) using Amex test simulation tools and customized test plans.
claims.quote: American Express issuers must perform host and payment product certification, collaborating with the American Express certification teams, leveraging test simulation tools and customized test plans.
claims.title: American Express Certification
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Host certification activities listed: unattended testing, telecommunication connectivity validation, message and file validation.

claims.claim: The Network Specifications required for host certification are gated behind the Knowledge Base login; nothing technical is public.
claims.quote: For all host certification efforts, American Express Global Network Specifications are required. To view these Network Specifications, Log in to Knowledge Base
claims.title: American Express Certification
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: For value-added capabilities (EMV, contactless, mobile) the published process is: contact relationship manager, review messaging scripts, attend specification walkthrough, execute testing, coordinate production install/beta.

claims.claim: Amex host certification is an 8-step, representative-led process ending in an Authorization and Settlement Test Plan/Certification Summary before production.
claims.quote: American Express issues an Authorization and Settlement Test Plan/Certification Summary designating successful completion of host certification
claims.title: EMV Testing and Certification White Paper: Current Global Payment Network Requirements for the U.S. Acquiring Community, Version 5.0
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Section 2.4. Steps: notify Amex, Amex initiates project request, assigns certification resource, reviews process and test plan, participant executes test plan, Amex issues summary, participant moves to production. Also: 'Merchants, acquirers, processors and others (ISOs, ISVs, VARs) can also register on Amex Enabled'. Document says input came from American Express; date 'September 2023' with file stamp 09292023.

claims.claim: Amex Level 3 device certification requires prior acquirer host certification, current EMVCo L1/L2 (Amex Expresspay L2 for contactless), PCI approval and an EMVCo-qualified L3 test tool.
claims.quote: Acquirer host certification. EMVCo Level 1 and EMVCo Level 2* (American Express/Expresspay Level 2* in case of contactless) certification status must be completed/current
claims.title: EMV Testing and Certification White Paper: Current Global Payment Network Requirements for the U.S. Acquiring Community, Version 5.0
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Section 3.5.2. Also 'PCI approval is required for all POS devices to complete L3 certification' and 'Use of a EMVCo L3 qualified test tool is required'. L3 process: unattended self-testing then attended testing with Amex; 'American Express issues certification letter & provides Live Terminal parameters'.

claims.claim: Amex offers a self-accreditation route, the POS Certification Participant Program (CPP), letting qualifying acquirers and processors self-test devices to streamline end-to-end certification.
claims.quote: The American Express POS Certification Participant Program (CPP) is available to acquirer and acquirer processors interested in conducting self-testing of devices
claims.title: EMV Testing and Certification White Paper: Current Global Payment Network Requirements for the U.S. Acquiring Community, Version 5.0
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Section 3.5.4. Program requirements are not published; 'Please contact the American Express representative to receive more information about the program (CPP).'

claims.claim: Amex provides its own host simulator (ATS) free of charge for certification testing; processors using another simulator must meet the Approved Solution Provider Program requirements at their own cost.
claims.quote: The American Express Test System ("ATS") is an approved host simulator available at no cost to merchants and processors
claims.title: EMV Testing and Certification White Paper: Current Global Payment Network Requirements for the U.S. Acquiring Community, Version 5.0
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Section 3.5.5. Amex's own Approved Solution Provider Program list (27 Jan 2021) names BCTC, FIME and FIS Open Test Solutions tools against AEIPS 6.4 / Expresspay 4.0 test plans: https://network.americanexpress.com/globalnetwork/dam/jcr:4016710d-8bae-4dfa-90d4-1e11b1652996/Acquiring%20Test%20Tool%20%20ASP%20Program%20Approved%20List-01272021.pdf

claims.claim: Service providers (processors, gateways, terminal and card vendors, labs, tool makers) join via the AMEX Enabled programme in three steps: register the company under click-through NDA and T&Cs, enrol a Knowledge Base user, log into the AMEX Enabled Dashboard.
claims.quote: Register your company with the AMEX Enabled program. Provide company details and main company contact information. Accept Non-Disclosure Agreement and Terms and Conditions.
claims.title: Partners | Service Providers | American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Register Company button resolves to a Salesforce-hosted form at https://aegns-prism.my.site.com/amexenabledv2/s/register-company-new. www.amexenabled.com redirects to this page. Product portfolios: SafeKey ACS/3DS Server, Click to Pay SRCi, AETS tokenization, card issuing/personalization, mobile issuing, contactless terminals (Level 2 Expresspay), payment platforms, test labs, test tools, QR, integrated payments providers, transit.

claims.claim: There is no fee to register for AMEX Enabled.
claims.quote: There are no fees charged to register for the AMEX Enabled Program.
claims.title: AMEX Enabled Frequently Asked Questions
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Document dated June 2022. Same FAQ: T&Cs and NDA 'are completed by click through acceptance as part of your company registration process'; registration help at AmexEnabled@aexp.com. No certification fee or timeline is stated anywhere in the programme documents.

claims.claim: AMEX Enabled dashboard access requires a Knowledge Base ID; once registration is approved, additional users are invited (up to five extra users per the overview), and contracts are executed digitally.
claims.quote: Once registration is approved, invite or enroll additional users with a Knowledge Base ID to gain access to the AMEX Enabled Dashboard.
claims.title: AMEX Enabled Service Provider Program
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Document dated June 2022. Dashboard features described (Vendor claims): 'Enjoy digital contracts sent, delivered, complete via DocuSign', a Messaging Center with Amex Product Specialists, and 'Invite five additional users'. The overview counts '800+ SERVICE PROVIDERS' versus '1200+' on the 2026 web page.

claims.claim: AMEX Enabled registration is not itself approval: a product must still pass certification before an issuer, acquirer or provider may use it on the network.
claims.quote: Products or services will require certification to be allowed for use by an Issuer, Acquirer or Provider on the American Express Global Network.
claims.title: AMEX Enabled Service Provider Program
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Footnote 1. Same footnote: 'Any listing, designation, approval or certification by American Express does not constitute a guarantee, endorsement, or warranty'.

claims.claim: Amex markets AMEX Enabled as a certified-vendor directory of over 1,200 service providers across 17 product portfolios and 45+ products.
claims.quote: join over 1200 Service Providers who have developed, certified and deployed their products and services for use on the American Express Network
claims.title: Partners | Service Providers | American Express
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Self-reported count; June 2022 overview PDF said 800+. Certified providers may issue a pre-written press release and use the AMEX Enabled logo.

claims.claim: Third parties at the merchant POS (ISOs, ISVs, VARs, iPOS, ESOs, mPOS/SoftPOS, PSP/processor aggregators, merchant servicers) are registered through the Integrated Payments Providers (IPP) programme, an AMEX Enabled track.
claims.quote: Vendors may include: Merchant Services (MS) Independent Sales Organizations (ISO) Independent Software Vendors (ISV) Value Added Resellers (VAR)
claims.title: Partners | Service Providers | American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: List continues: iPOS, Encryption Services Organizations (ESO), Mobile Point Of Sale (mPOS) / SoftPOS, PSP/Processor Aggregator. Amex does not publish a separate third-party-agent registry comparable to Visa's TPA or Mastercard's TPP registration; ISO registration in OptBlue is handled by the Participant (see Global Payments claim).

claims.claim: The IPP programme charges no dues or fees and is framed as a relationship and specification-access channel rather than a licence.
claims.quote: At this time we are not associating any dues or fees with the initiative.
claims.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Integrated Payments Providers Program
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: FAQ dated September 2018 (copyright 2019); still linked from the 2026 IPP page. Q6 'What does registration cost?'. Contact: PaymentVendorRelations@aexp.com.

claims.claim: The IPP onboarding path is five published steps: register online, accept T&Cs, enrol users with a GNSweb ID, log into the AMEX Enabled Dashboard for specs and policies, then complete testing and certification.
claims.quote: Enroll one or more users with a GNSweb ID and password to access the AMEX Enabled Dashboard.
claims.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Integrated Payments Providers Program
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Q7 'How do I get started?'. Step 5: 'Complete testing and certification of your solution.' The current IPP page says the programme 'provides a central point of contact for technical and specification guidance, certification assistance, and production support' and covers POS devices, e-commerce (SafeKey/3DS, card-on-file) and host platforms (authorizations, submissions, direct connection, online PIN).

claims.claim: SafeKey (3-D Secure) ACS and 3DS Server providers certify via a five-step AMEX Enabled flow: register company (ticking the SafeKey ACS/MPI box), enrol users, access dashboard, enrol product, then certify with the SafeKey Certification Team.
claims.quote: Complete the AMEX Enabled company registration form, ensuring that the relevant SafeKey ACS/MPI checkbox is ticked
claims.title: SafeKey Provider Enrollment Instructions
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Document dated September 2023. Version uplifts (2.1 to 2.2/2.3) use an Uplift Questionnaire emailed to safekey.certification@aexp.com; registration help via gns.user.services@aexp.com. No timeline stated: 'The SafeKey Certification Team will be in touch with next steps.'

claims.claim: Test laboratories seeking AMEX Enabled accreditation must already hold EMVCo accreditation and the relevant EMVCo working-group audit (CAWG for cards, SEWG for security, TAWG for terminals) before registering.
claims.quote: Valid EMVCo Accreditation for L1 Contact and Contactless Type Approval Valid EMVCo Card Approval Working Group (CAWG) Audit
claims.title: AMEX Enabled Test Laboratory Accreditation Program
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: File stamp 2018-02-01; marked 'AXP Public'. Physical card labs must demonstrate ISO 7810/7816 testing; Expresspay Level 2 terminal labs need EMVCo Contactless Type Approval accreditation and a TAWG audit.

claims.claim: Card, mobile and terminal products reach Amex approval only through security and functional testing at an Amex-accredited laboratory (for example Applus+), layered on EMVCo approvals.
claims.quote: AMEX-compliant products must pass an AMEX approval process that requires security evaluations and functional tests performed by an AMEX-accredited laboratory.
claims.title: American Express Certification | Applus+ Laboratories
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Lab lists AEIPS 4.5 (contact) and Expresspay 4.1 (contactless) card type approvals and 'AMEX Terminal Type Approval L2'. Third-party lab describing the network's process.

claims.claim: Payment facilitators join Amex acceptance by registering through an OptBlue Participant, not with Amex directly, and Amex charges no registration fee.
claims.quote: American Express does not charge a registration fee to participate in OptBlue®
claims.title: Payments Facilitator Acceptance of American Express Cards
claims.publisher: American Express Global Merchant and Network Services
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Document dated October 2024. First requirement: 'Register as a Payment Facilitator with American Express through an OptBlue Participant'. Eligibility headline: payment facilitators with less than $250MM in annual American Express charge volume.

claims.claim: Amex defines a payment facilitator as the merchant of record for its program merchants and caps what a PayFac may sponsor: no single merchant above $1MM Amex volume and no sub-PayFacs.
claims.quote: Do not sponsor individual merchants with greater than $1MM in annual American Express charge volume
claims.title: Payments Facilitator Acceptance of American Express Cards
claims.publisher: American Express Global Merchant and Network Services
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'Do not act as a sponsor for another Payment Facilitator' and 'American Express defines a Payment Facilitator as a provider of Payment Services that accepts the American Express Card as the merchant of record'. The $1MM figure predates the April 2026 threshold change on the OptBlue pages.

claims.claim: OptBlue Participants are bound by non-public Operating Regulations that cap which merchants they may sign; the U.S. acquiring threshold rose to $3,000,000 ECV effective April 17, 2026.
claims.quote: Effective April 17, 2026, the merchant acquiring threshold in the U.S. has been increased to $3,000,000.
claims.title: OptBlue Sales Agent | American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same page: 'OptBlue Participants may only acquire prospective merchants that meet the Estimated Annual Charge Volume (ECV) program limits as outlined in the Operating Regulations.' The Operating Regulations themselves are not published. Threshold excludes Puerto Rico and USVI; no threshold for charity, healthcare, education, government, insurance, residential rent, utilities, online gambling/games of value.

claims.claim: Payment facilitators and third-party service providers can only ride OptBlue under a Participant whose PayFac sales channel Amex has certified; Amex marks such Participants on its public list.
claims.quote: Payment Facilitators registered for the OptBlue program under a Participant with a certified Payment Facilitator sales channel
claims.title: Credit Card Processing for Small Businesses | OptBlue American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Public list of 30+ Participants (Adyen, Bank of America, Chase, Elavon, Fiserv, Global Payments, PayPal*, Square, Stripe, Worldpay* etc.); asterisk marks certified PayFac channel. Also: 'Only approved and certified OptBlue Participants are permitted to acquire in certain Online Gambling and Games of Value segments.'

claims.claim: Amex publishes no process for an acquirer or processor to become an OptBlue Participant; the public routes are merchant sign-up via an existing Participant or a phone number for direct acceptance.
claims.quote: If your business is not eligible for OptBlue or is interested in accepting American Express Cards directly with American Express, please call 1-866-847-0890.
claims.title: Credit Card Processing for Small Businesses | OptBlue American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Merchant eligibility: 'U.S. businesses that have American Express Estimated Annual Charge Volume (ECV) of less than $3MM per year may be eligible to accept through OptBlue.' The Sales Agent page is a resource hub for agents already working under Participants, not an enrolment path.

claims.claim: In practice, OptBlue ISO registration is administered by the Participant acquirer: Global Payments assigns each ISO a registration number tied to its Participant Sales Entity, and merchants are boarded under that number.
claims.quote: This number identifies the individual ISOs under an acquirer (Participant Sales Entity - PSE) and is assigned by Global Payments
claims.title: AMEX Merchant Registration (Express Boarding and Servicing help)
claims.publisher: Global Payments (Express Boarding and Servicing documentation)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Same page: participating clients 'can enter into contracts with eligible merchants in the United States' and need not register merchants signed as ESA or AMEX-Direct. Processor-side practitioner documentation, not an Amex document.

claims.claim: OptBlue was launched in February 2014 with six acquirers and scaled through ISOs sponsored by those acquirers; within a year a dozen acquirers and 'hundreds' of ISOs were enrolled.
claims.quote: At least a dozen major bank card acquirers and merchant processors now offer OptBlue, up from six when AmEx announced the program in February 2014
claims.title: AmEx Claims 400,000 Small Merchants Through Its ISO-Driven OptBlue Program
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Historical; predates the 2025 Capital One/Discover transaction. Article gives no acquirer certification detail.

claims.claim: Large processors describe themselves as 'certified processors of American Express', meaning certified for both authorization and submission (settlement) connections.
claims.quote: J.P. Morgan, as a certified processor of American Express is capable in providing integration to supporting existing merchant accounts for both authorizations and submissions
claims.title: American Express - Partner Integration | J.P. Morgan
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Partner-side claim; no onboarding steps given beyond a 'Request more info' button.

claims.claim: In Amex's April 2026 Merchant Operating Guide, a 'Merchant Services Provider' is defined as an entity authorized under OptBlue, or a payment facilitator, to accept charges from a merchant, formalising the two indirect acquiring routes.
claims.quote: An Entity authorized under the American Express OptBlue® Program to accept Charges from a Merchant pursuant to an Agreement
claims.title: Merchant Operating Guide, All Regions, April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Document dated April 2026, 120 pages. Also defines Payment Facilitator as 'formerly referred to as Payment Aggregator, Payment Service Provider or PSP', and requires 'all Merchants and their Merchant Services Provider to be Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) compliant'.

claims.claim: Merchant POS systems must be certified with Amex for chip acceptance; an uncertified POS shifts counterfeit and lost/stolen chargeback liability to the merchant.
claims.quote: The Merchant has not certified the POS system with American Express to accept Chip Transactions or Chip and PIN Transactions.
claims.title: Merchant Operating Guide, All Regions, April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Listed as one of three conditions under which Amex may exercise chargeback or terminate for chip liability. Cannabis (Canada only) requires a signed due diligence checklist and certification form approved by Amex and a new Service Establishment number.

claims.claim: Amex's U.S. Merchant Reference Guide makes conformance to its Technical Specifications a condition of connecting to the network for merchants, processors and terminal providers alike.
claims.quote: Merchants, Processors, Terminal Providers, and others must conform to the Technical Specifications in order to connect to and transact on the Network.
claims.title: Merchant Reference Guide U.S., October 2021
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Document dated October 2021 (latest public version found; marked confidential on each page yet hosted publicly). Section 2.5. Merchants remain liable for third parties they enlist (service providers/processors, terminal providers, vendors, Covered Parties).

claims.claim: The Amex for Developers portal describes a six-stage journey: explore products, reach out for access, sign contracts if required, sign up and create a project, test in sandbox, then promote to production.
claims.quote: If needed, you will be required to sign contractual agreements to receive full access to our products.
claims.title: High-Level Process | American Express Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Portal is a JavaScript app; content read from its content host https://icm.aexp-static.com/Internet/EnterpriseAPIPortal/documentation/content/how-it-works.md. Also: 'Some products are not publicly listed on our website due to security reasons' and 'For some of our public products, the Sandbox APIs are automatically accessible without reaching out to us.' 'Last Updated: June 1, 2026'.

claims.claim: Developer onboarding runs sandbox to production through project-level To-Do items (certificate upload, OAuth details, questionnaire) with Requested/Approved states; production promotion repeats the review and may require accepting legal terms.
claims.quote: After validation in Sandbox, you will be able to upgrade to Production. If your Sandbox integration is in an "Approved" state
claims.title: Getting Started | American Express Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Read from https://icm.aexp-static.com/Internet/EnterpriseAPIPortal/documentation/content/getting-started.md. 'Once you submit the required information, the product will be in Requested state. We will review your request and approve it.' Client ID and Client Secret appear on the project dashboard. No review SLA or fee is published.

claims.claim: Developer portal sign-up is self-service at developer.americanexpress.com/signup but requires a company name, a memorised security code and email one-time-code verification; support is via support@devmail.americanexpress.com.
claims.quote: Enter your business/company's name when prompted. This is a required field; otherwise, you cannot proceed with the registration
claims.title: How to Register | American Express Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Read from the content host how-to-register.md. What's New (Nov 2023): 'Users will now be required to create a security code at signup.' No account was created for this study.

claims.claim: The developer portal uses role-based access: Owners (company level) create projects and request production keys, Admins manage a project, and Developers can only request sandbox access.
claims.quote: Developers have the Project permission level, enabling them to manage Sandbox access and view documentation within the project.
claims.title: Access Guide | American Express Developers
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Permissions table: Production Keys and Access is true for Owner and Admin, false for Developer. Read from the content host access-guide.md; 'Last Updated: June 1, 2026'.

claims.claim: Amex's fintech on-ramp uses a sponsor model: through the i2c agreement fintechs get pre-certified processors and bank issuing BIN sponsors instead of licensing directly.
claims.quote: fintechs will get access to pre-certified partners, including bank issuing BIN sponsors, making it faster and simpler to bring their payment innovations to market
claims.title: American Express Increases Speed for Fintechs to Launch Cards on the Amex Network, Powered by i2c
claims.publisher: American Express Global Network Services (Business Wire release)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Amex press release on its own site; date per the release. Also: the network is 'open for business with fintechs by creating a plug-and-play onboarding platform'. Examples: Keo (Mexico), Bancrédito (Puerto Rico). Predates the 2025 Capital One/Discover close.

claims.claim: American Banker reports the Agile Partner Platform (APP) as GNS's curated fintech entry route, built on sponsor banks (Celtic, Evolve, First Electronic) and cloud processors (i2c, CoreCard), with Amex stressing selectivity.
claims.quote: a power strip that fintechs can plug into to access American Express's broader electrical grid
claims.title: 'We are picky': Inside Amex's fintech strategy
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Mohammed Badi, president of GNS, quoted: 'We are picky about who we partner with.' The fetch tool summarised (not verbatim) that a traditional 18-month bank integration falls to roughly two months on APP; treat that timeline as reported, not quoted. More than 10 APP partners at the time.

claims.claim: Card-issuing platforms (Lithic, May 2025; Marqeta, Feb 2025) have been admitted to the Agile Partnership Platform so their fintech clients can issue on the Amex network without a direct Amex licence.
claims.quote: We are very pleased to welcome Lithic to our Agile Partnership Platform, which helps fintechs and other industry disruptors launch payment products
claims.title: Lithic Expands Platform to Offer More Payment Options for Fintechs on the American Express Network
claims.publisher: Lithic (press release; quote from Will Stredwick, SVP and GM of GNS North America, American Express)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Postdates the May 18, 2025 Capital One/Discover close by four days. Marqeta, per PYMNTS 2025-02-26: 'leveraging the American Express Agile Partnership platform, which enables FinTechs and other partners to launch cards on the American Express network' (https://www.pymnts.com/earnings/2025/marqeta-announces-transactpay-acquisition-and-ceo-transition-as-processing-volumes-leap-29/). BusinessWire copy returned 403.

claims.claim: Fintech programmes on the Amex network are issued by a sponsor bank (for example First Electronic Bank for Cardless), confirming Amex requires a licensed bank issuer behind fintech cards.
claims.quote: Cards are issued by First Electronic Bank, and cardholders manage their accounts through the Cardless app.
claims.title: Fintech Cardless taps Amex network
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: William Stredwick quoted: 'Our agreement with Cardless is yet another way we're working with fintechs to continue increasing the scale and relevance of the American Express network.' Predates the 2025 Capital One/Discover close.

claims.claim: Amex's public fintech page offers only positioning ('speed to market', customisable product lines) and no application, eligibility or sponsor-bank information.
claims.quote: Speed to Market with American Express' flexible, agile approach.
claims.title: Partners | Fintechs | American Express
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: The Agile Partnership Platform is not named anywhere on the public GNS site; it appears only in press releases and trade press.

claims.claim: ATM acquirers join Amex cash access through market-by-market bank partnerships; Amex publishes no global ATM-acquirer application process and says processes vary by market.
claims.quote: Application processes, cash limits and, ATM functionality may vary from market to market and card type.
claims.title: Cash Access with American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Vendor figures on the same page: cash access at 'more than 1.5 million ATMs worldwide' via ATM networks 'in more than 150 countries'. Benefits offered to ATM acquirers are marketing assets and ATM Locator listing; no fee, certification or interface detail.

claims.claim: Post-signing onboarding support for Network Participants is delivered as webinars and online modules (Compliance covering the BOP, Operations & Services, Chargeback & Disputes) requested through the Amex representative or PartnerLearning@aexp.com.
claims.quote: American Express Network Participants are eligible to request and register for trainings, please contact your American Express representative
claims.title: Partners | Backing Our Partners | American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Compliance training: 'six modules that cover more than fifty Network policies'. Training registration links resolve to the gated Knowledge Base.

claims.claim: Once licensed, participants enrol in individual network services through a 'Service Enrollment' function inside the gated Knowledge Base, which also hosts a Participant Directory.
claims.quote: Find out more about each service available and enrol directly for the services you require all in one place.
claims.title: Partners | Integrated Payments Providers Program | American Express
